messages.subject: access to shiny server
parts:
Hi,

I am a green bird in Linux and web server. Recently I am trying to deploy a web application using R for my website. After some search on internet, I decided to use ubuntu 12.04 and shiny-server for setting up my website. I followed the instruction in the website https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-server, and it worked perfectly well until I tried to access it. I used the examples given in the website and I am able to access it via http://localhost:3838/examples/. My wlan0 inet addr is 192.168.10.103, and I can also access it via http://192.168.10.103:3838/examples/. But how can my friend access it? I tried to replace the wlan0 inet addr with my ip address and it does not work.
Thanks for you help!

Best,
Xu

messages.author: 55771919c42cb6a1
messages.subject: Re: access to shiny server
parts:
Is your friend connected to the same local network? The address 192.168.10.103 is an address which will be visible within your local network, but it won't be visible from the rest of the internet. It sounds like you are connected to a wireless router. You can think of the router as joining two networks: the internet, and a local network for your computers. Computers on the internet won't be able to connect to servers on the local network.

If you want to run your own server that is visible on the internet, the best route is to use a hosting service like Amazon EC2.

-Winston
